problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-{7}^{x}+3?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={7}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/283470740585f9ddba5e81ccf2c2fcb7d34d339ab26cb0ea35aae2bac4b85e1b.png)

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{7}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/66a1dd2866d56323de98e2ec0bf665ebb20d7d770cbd8691a825749d660f125d.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $3$ units up to give $y=-{7}^{x}+3.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(0,2)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/7a1b3b562e4489b8b649f20d3133960dda7e5213827adb2bf7fd94e6659a64c4.png)
